title: PUSHtap: PIM-based In-Memory HTAP with Unified Data Storage Format
problem: Hybrid transaction/analytical processing (HTAP) systems cannot simultaneously achieve workload-specific optimization, performance isolation, and data freshness because OLTP demands row-store format while OLAP demands column-store format, and existing solutions (single format, multi-instance with rebuilding, or mixed delta-store) compromise at least one goal.
method: PUSHtap maps HTAP rows to the CPU's interleaved access dimension (ADE) and columns to the PIM's localized access dimension (IDE) in a single-instance DRAM store. A compact aligned format uses a bin-packing algorithm with a tunable threshold to group columns of similar width into parts, minimizing zero-padding while preserving alignment for both CPU and PIM bandwidth efficiency. Block-circulant placement rotates column-to-PIM-device mapping every 1024-row block, ensuring uniform PIM parallelism load balance across all columns. MVCC is implemented with a data region and delta region; snapshotting encodes row visibility as compact bitmaps that are written to each device in parallel, and defragmentation is offloaded to PIM units when row width exceeds a computed threshold. A modified memory controller adds a scheduler and polling module to support fine-grained interleaved CPU/PIM concurrent access, with a two-phase load/compute OLAP execution model that limits CPU access blocking to 300 microseconds per load phase.

title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
problem: Serving LLMs on long sequences (>64k tokens) is bottlenecked by attention: quadratic complexity during prefill and linear KV cache memory pressure during decode. No existing system addresses both stages simultaneously in a unified framework.
method: LServe unifies structured block-sparse attention patterns in a single framework. For static sparsity: half of attention heads are designated as streaming heads (attend only to sink tokens and recent local window, Λ-shaped mask) identified offline via DuoAttention's optimization-based gating. A fused CUDA kernel handles both streaming and dense heads in one pass for both prefill and decode. For dynamic sparsity (decode only): hierarchical paging introduces a two-level abstraction where logical pages (fine-grained, NL tokens) are used for importance scoring while physical pages (NP = g*NL tokens) hold the actual quantized KV data. Page importance is max-pooled from logical page scores (query dot product with per-logical-page kmax/kmin statistics). Reusable page selection exploits temporal locality: the same page selection result is shared across a chunk of consecutive decode steps. All sparsity patterns are unified in block-sparse attention kernels with W4A8KV4 quantization.

title: TileLink: Generating Efficient Compute-Communication Overlapping Kernels using Tile-Centric Primitives
problem: Distributed LLM training and inference require overlapping compute with inter-GPU communication (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter) to hide network latency. Operator decomposition is easy but leaves performance on the table; fusing communication into compute kernels is effective but requires expert CUDA/NVSHMEM code that is error-prone and non-portable.
method: TileLink has a frontend and a backend. The frontend exposes tile-centric primitives: producer_tile_notify/consumer_tile_wait synchronize tile-level data readiness; peer_tile_notify/peer_tile_wait coordinate cross-rank tile dependencies; tile_push_data/tile_pull_data transfer tiles between devices; rank_copy_data/rank_notify/rank_wait handle rank-level collective coordination. The backend performs tile-centric mapping in three stages: (1) shape mapping assigns tile dimensions to compute and communication workloads; (2) rank mapping determines which GPU rank computes/receives each tile via affine transforms (static) or runtime lookup tables (dynamic); (3) channel mapping assigns each tile to an NVLink/InfiniBand channel. The backend compiles these mappings to PTX via Triton extended with NVSHMEM primitives, producing fused kernels that interleave compute threads and communication threads within a single CUDA kernel.

title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
problem: MoE LLMs suffer large accuracy degradation at INT3 weight quantization; existing calibration-free methods yield poor accuracy and existing INT3 kernels lack measured throughput gains at batch size > 1.
method: Calibration-free HQQ-based INT3 quantization combined with a mixture of adaptive low-rank compensators (SVD-based residual reconstruction). Compensator rank is selected per-layer based on: (1) dense vs sparse layer type, (2) weight kurtosis, (3) expert activation frequency. Iterative joint optimization of quantized weights and compensators. Both weights and compensators are INT3-packed. Custom W3A16 Tensor Core GeMM kernel with zero-bit-waste INT3 packing, binary manipulation I2F dequantization, async global weight loading, and support for batch size > 1.

title: DECA: A Near-Core LLM Decompression Accelerator Grounded on a 3D Roofline Model
problem: LLM inference on CPU servers (Intel Sapphire Rapids with AMX TMUL and HBM) is bottlenecked not by memory bandwidth or matrix compute throughput, but by AVX vector decompression overhead: decompressing quantized (BF8, MXFP4) and sparsified weight tiles in software consumes over 95% of dynamic instructions per core, and even 4x more vector (AVX) throughput is insufficient to eliminate this bottleneck for highly compressed models.
method: DECA is a near-core ML model decompression accelerator placed alongside each CPU core and connected via memory-mapped interface sharing the L2 TLB. Its microarchitecture is a three-stage pipeline: (1) Dequantization using a LUT array (L parallel 256-entry LUTs) that converts low-bit quantized values (1–8 bit) to BF16; (2) Expansion that de-sparsifies data by inserting zeros at bitmask-specified positions using a crossbar (XBAR) controlled by Parallel Prefix Sum-generated expansion indices from a bitmask queue; (3) Scaling that applies per-group scale factors for group quantization. Two duplicated Loader+TOut register pairs enable hardware double buffering between DECA and the TMUL. A new ISA extension called TEPL (Tile External Preprocess and Load) eliminates per-iteration memory fences by out-of-order invocation of DECA — TEPL instructions are issued speculatively like loads, and the core is squash-safe because DECA never writes memory state. The design methodology is grounded in a novel 3D Roof-Surface analytical model extending the 2D roofline to add a vector-throughput axis (AIXV = matrix ops per vector op), which correctly predicts that highly compressed kernels are VEC-bound, not MEM-bound.
